issues.legal_issue: A court supervising a liquidation sale may reopen a sale that remains subject to confirmation when a higher offer indicates that competitive bidding may produce a better price for those interested in the estate.
material_facts: An asset in winding-up proceedings was sold through a court-supervised auction, subject to the court’s confirmation.
After one bidder was declared the highest bidder, another bidder offered more, and the court allowed further competitive bidding.
A still higher offer was made before the sale was finally confirmed.
The sale proceeds would benefit the company, its creditors and its workmen.
issues.conclusion: The court held that the company judge had properly exercised discretion to reopen the auction and allow further bidding; the appeal against the order requiring a fresh open auction was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Companies Act, the court’s sanction of a liquidation sale must be exercised judicially, having regard to the interests of the company and its creditors. As held in Navalkha and Sons v. Ramanuja Das, acceptance of an offer subject to court confirmation gives the bidder no vested right to automatic confirmation, and the court must be satisfied that the price is reasonable in light of market value. Kayjay Industries (P.) Ltd. v. Asnew Drums (P.) Ltd. recognizes that court sales may not produce the best price and that the court may consider whether postponement could secure a better one. The requirement in Radhy Shyam v. Shyam Behari Singh, under Order 21, Rule 90 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, that inadequacy be caused by material irregularity or fraud concerns setting aside a sale under that rule; fraud is not necessary in every case for a court to exercise its discretion over a liquidation sale that remains subject to confirmation.

rule.if: liquidation_sale_appeal and sale_subject_to_confirmation and higher_offer_made and estate_stakeholders_benefit_from_competition

predicates.liquidation_sale_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a court-supervised sale of an asset in winding-up proceedings.
predicates.sale_subject_to_confirmation: The sale terms make the sale subject to the court’s confirmation.
predicates.higher_offer_made: A bidder offers more than the amount previously offered for the asset while the sale remains before the court.
predicates.estate_stakeholders_benefit_from_competi: A better sale price would benefit people or entities whose interests are served by the proceeds of the liquidation sale.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a liquidation sale subject to confirmation, a higher offer is made, and competitive bidding may benefit estate stakeholders, the court may reopen the sale for competitive bidding.

issues.legal_issue: A court may set aside a court-supervised sale and order a fresh auction despite payment and execution of a conveyance when the sale terms preserve the court’s power to do so and a higher offer shows that renewed competition may secure a better price.
material_facts: After an earlier direction for an auction limited to two bidders, one bidder won with the highest bid and paid the amount required; a conveyance was executed and registered.
The conveyance remained subject to the outcome of the appeal, and the published sale conditions allowed the court to alter the sale terms and set aside the sale even after confirmation and payment.
The other bidder later offered a higher price and produced demand drafts for the shortfall.
The court considered that the earlier auction had been limited to two bidders, that the property could fetch more, and that the parties were prepared to bid again.
issues.conclusion: The court set aside the sale and directed a fresh auction, fixing an upset price and allowing the existing deposit to remain in place pending the auction.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the principle stated in its earlier ruling in this matter that an open auction should remain open to intending bidders so that it can secure the most remunerative price, and that meaningful court supervision can guard against underbidding and inadequate proceeds. It also relied on the published sale conditions reserving power to modify the terms and to set aside a sale even after confirmation and payment, and on the appellate direction that any conveyance would abide by the appeal’s result. Although repeated disturbance of a court auction may discourage bidders, the court held that the circumstances—including a higher offer and the restricted earlier auction—justified a fresh sale.

rule.if: appeal_concerning_court_sale and sale_terms_reserve_power_to_set_aside and conveyance_subject_to_appeal and higher_offer_demonstrates_price_potential and parties_willing_to_bid_again

predicates.appeal_concerning_court_sale: The proceeding is an appeal concerning the validity or reopening of a court-supervised sale.
predicates.sale_terms_reserve_power_to_set_aside: The published sale terms reserve the court’s power to alter the sale terms or set aside the sale even after confirmation and payment.
predicates.conveyance_subject_to_appeal: Any conveyance made to the successful bidder remains subject to the outcome of the pending appeal.
predicates.higher_offer_demonstrates_price_potentia: A later offer exceeds the winning bid and indicates that renewed competition may obtain a better price.
predicates.parties_willing_to_bid_again: The bidders are prepared to participate in another auction.

issues.definition: If an appeal concerns a court-supervised sale, the sale terms preserve the power to set it aside, the conveyance remains subject to the appeal, a higher offer indicates further price potential, and the bidders will bid again, the court may set aside the sale and direct a fresh auction.
